Expectation1: Look out for each other's safety and well-being
Situation1: One sibling is about to cross the street without looking for oncoming traffic.
Situation2: It seems your friend is confused about the meeting spot, and you need to send a message right now to confirm it.
Story: I was standing on the busy sidewalk with my younger brother, waiting for the light to change. My phone buzzed in my pocket—my friend, Sam, was texting again, clearly confused about where we were supposed to meet. He’d already messaged twice, and I knew if I didn’t reply right away, he’d probably get frustrated or think I was ignoring him. At the same time, I saw my brother inching forward, his eyes fixed on something across the street, not paying attention to the traffic. I felt a surge of panic—Mom always said I had to look out for him, make sure he was safe. But Sam was counting on me to clear things up, and I didn’t want to let him down either. My hand hovered over my phone, torn between grabbing my brother’s arm and quickly typing out a message. My heart pounded as I realized I couldn’t do both at once, and I was stuck, caught between being a good sibling and a good friend.
